JobEvent.description:
A job event of `GET /events`: the SSE event name is `kind`, the `data:` line is this object.

Stored events (`state`, `progress`, `log`) have the SSE id `<job_id>:<seq>`. A reconnecting browser resends the
last one as `Last-Event-ID`, and the stream replays the stored events after it. Previews are not stored in
`job_events` and never replayed: a `preview` has no `id:` line and repeats the `seq` of the job's latest stored
event, so `Last-Event-ID` always names a stored event. After a stream opens or reconnects (after its replay), the
core sends the latest kept preview of each running job the stream covers once; later previews follow live.

data.description: By `kind`. `state`: `state` (a JobState), plus where set: `worker_id` (`leased`), `reason` (why the job was queued again, cancelled or failed after its last attempt), `outputs` (`succeeded`: the output SHA-256 values in completion order) and `error` (a JobError: `failed`, or `cancelled` while running). `progress`: a Progress (`phase`, `step`, `total_steps`, `percent`). `preview`: `media_type` and `data_base64` (the frame as base64), as the worker sent them; the core does not check them, the shipped worker sends `image/png`, `image/jpeg` or `image/webp` of at most 256 KiB. `log`: `message`, a sentence for people. Log rows that cores before migration 0002 stored for an upload also carry `output` (`name`, `sha256`, `media_type`, `size_bytes`), and replay still sends them as stored; uploads are now the job's outputs, and workers may not send `output`.
data.title: Data

seq.description: Per-job sequence number of the stored events, starting at 1; a `preview` repeats the latest one
seq.title: Seq

SystemEvent.description:
A non-job event of `GET /events`: the SSE event name is `kind`, the `data:` line is this object.

Only a stream without `job_id` carries them. They have no id, are not stored and never replayed, so a stream
gets only those published while it is open; reload `GET /system` or `GET /models` whenever the stream opens.
`engine`: progress or a state change of engine provisioning, with the engine as `GET /system` reports it.
`model`: progress or a state change of a model install, also a removal or an eviction (`absent`).

delete.description:
Delete an asset for good: its record, its file and the job output records of it. There is no recycle bin.

Jobs that made or used it keep their state and events but no longer list it as an output; assets made from it keep
their provenance, whose `parents` still name it. Refused with 409 while a job that has not ended (awaiting approval,
queued or running) uses it as an input, and while its file stays open elsewhere, for example in a player.

post.description:
Start provisioning the engine (the Setup view's retry) unless it is ready or already provisioning.

Returns the engine's state; progress and the result follow as `engine` events on `GET /events`.

200.description: Server-sent events. Each message has an `event:` line with the event's kind and a `data:` line with one JSON object: a JobEvent for the job event kinds (`state`, `progress`, `preview`, `log`), a SystemEvent for the other kinds (`engine`: engine provisioning, `model`: model install progress, installs, removals and evictions). Stored job events have an `id:` line (`<job_id>:<seq>`). A stream first replays the stored events after `Last-Event-ID`; with `job_id` and without `Last-Event-ID`, the job's whole history. Previews and system events have no id and are never replayed: after its replay a stream sends the latest preview of each running job it covers once, and system events only while it is open. With `job_id` the stream carries only that job's events and ends after its final state; only a stream without `job_id` carries system events. A comment line (`: keepalive`) follows after 15 s without an event.

patch.description:
Change a host's settings. A new `text_encoder_variant` is switched in the background.

Checks first and refuses with 409 while a job runs on the host or a model is being installed, and when the
variant's files do not fit on the drive of the model store. `GET /hosts` shows the switch as the host's
`text_encoder_switch` while it runs or after it failed, and the new `text_encoder_variant` once it is done.

post.description:
Install a quantization with the shared files it needs, in the background.

Checks first and refuses with 409 when the model cannot be installed now: free disk space, the storage quota, an
install in progress, the licence's country exclusions. With a quota, the least recently used quantizations no job
needs are removed once the install is registered, so a failed download removes nothing. When the drive holds the
download only after removing them, the install is refused with `eviction_needed`, which lists them with their sizes;
sent again with each of them in `evict`, it removes them first, and they stay removed if the download fails.
Progress and the result follow as `model` events on `GET /events`; `GET /models` holds the state.

parameters.description: An installed quantization you agree to remove before the download, written `<model_id>:<quant>`; repeat it for each one that an `eviction_needed` refusal listed
parameters.name: evict

schema.title: Evict
